entities.summary: Menelaus, the legendary King of Sparta and husband of Helen, stands as a pivotal figure in Greek mythology and the foundational narrative of the Trojan War. His story, deeply embedded in the heroic age of Mycenaean Greece, transcends a mere personal saga, becoming a central catalyst for one of the most enduring epics in Western civilization. As the wronged husband whose wife, Helen, was abducted by Paris of Troy, Menelaus's quest for her retrieval ignited a decade-long conflict that reshaped the ancient world's understanding of heroism, honor, and divine intervention. His significance lies not only in his role as a warrior-king but as an archetype whose experiences underpin the very structure of epic poetry.
